pharm-immuno:tcell.e: Binds CD80/86 to block T-cell costimulation; used in kidney transplant.

pharm-immuno:cni.e: Also hirsutism; tacrolimus has more neurotoxicity and diabetes.

pharm-immuno:mtor.e: Blocks IL-2 signal transduction; used on drug-eluting stents.

pharm-immuno:antimetab.e: Converted to 6-MP, which xanthine oxidase and TPMT inactivate.

pharm-immuno:gc.e: Suppress cytokine transcription; also cause neutrophilia and lymphopenia.

pharm-immuno:gc.q: Stress-dose steroids are needed in long-term steroid users during:

pharm-immuno:cytokine.e: Metastatic renal cell carcinoma; capillary leak syndrome.

pharm-immuno:abs.e: NHL, CLL, RA, ITP; risk of HBV reactivation and PML.
Used in CLL and multiple sclerosis.

title.en: Boss case: After the kidney transplant

boss.case: A 45-year-old man received a deceased-donor kidney transplant 3 months ago. He takes tacrolimus, mycophenolate and prednisone. He now has new tremor and BP 160/95 mm Hg, and creatinine has risen from 1.2 to 1.8 mg/dL.

qs.e: Calcineurin dephosphorylates NFAT; blocking it ↓ IL-2 transcription.

qs.q: His tremor, hypertension and rising creatinine suggest:
qs.e: Check trough level; biopsy may be needed to exclude rejection.

qs.q: A drug that would raise tacrolimus levels:
qs.e: Clarithromycin and azole antifungals (ketoconazole) are CYP3A4 inhibitors; inducers lower levels and risk rejection.
Inhibits IMP dehydrogenase, which lymphocytes depend on; GI upset, cytopenias; teratogenic.

qs.q: Which immunosuppressant is nephro-sparing and may replace tacrolimus?
qs.e: Sirolimus (mTOR inhibitor) and belatacept are not nephrotoxic and are used to minimize calcineurin inhibitors; sirolimus causes hyperlipidemia and poor wound healing. Basiliximab is induction only.

steps.e: Cyclophosphamide is an alternative; mycophenolate is preferred in women wanting fertility.

steps.e: Mycophenolate is teratogenic; azathioprine is acceptable.
